title: Database & Data Engineering Readiness
description: Assess your understanding of distributed data pipelines, PySpark, Airflow DAGs, Snowflake data warehousing, Kafka streaming, and data modeling.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) and ELT (Extract, Load, Transform)?
options: In ELT, raw data is loaded directly into modern cloud data warehouses and transformed in-place using warehouse compute (SQL/dbt)
ETL does not require a database
ELT cannot process JSON or CSV files
ETL is only used for real-time streaming
questions.explanation: Modern cloud warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery) have massive parallel compute, allowing raw data ingestion followed by scalable in-warehouse ELT transformation.

questions.question: Why is the Apache Parquet file format preferred over CSV or JSON for big data analytics?
options: Parquet is columnar, provides efficient compression, and enables column pruning and predicate pushdown to skip reading unneeded data
Parquet files can be edited in Microsoft Notepad
Parquet files do not require schemas
Parquet is an uncompressed row-based text format
questions.explanation: Columnar storage allows analytics queries that only select a few columns to avoid scanning irrelevant columns, drastically reducing I/O and query time.

questions.question: In Apache Airflow, what does DAG stand for and what constraint does it enforce?
options: Directed Acyclic Graph; enforces that tasks execute with strict dependency direction and cannot have circular loops
Data Aggregation Gateway; limits queries to 1,000 rows
Distributed Async Generator; generates synthetic data
Database Action Group; handles database migrations
questions.explanation: A DAG defines tasks and their upstream/downstream relationships without circular feedback loops, ensuring predictable pipeline execution.

questions.question: In Apache Spark, what is the difference between a Transformation and an Action?
options: Transformations (like `map`, `filter`) are lazy and build an execution lineage DAG; Actions (like `count`, `collect`, `write`) trigger actual distributed execution
Transformations write data directly to disk immediately
Actions only run on the Spark driver node without workers
Transformations can only be run once per session
questions.explanation: Spark lazily evaluates transformations to optimize the entire query plan (via Catalyst optimizer) until an Action explicitly requests computation.

questions.question: What is 'Data Skew' in distributed computing (Spark/Hadoop) and how does it affect performance?
options: Data is unevenly distributed across partitions, causing a few straggler worker nodes to take dramatically longer than others
Data values contain typographical errors
The database timestamp clock is out of sync
The dataset has more columns than rows
questions.explanation: When partitioning keys are skewed (e.g. 80% of rows have key='USA'), the worker handling that key is overwhelmed while others sit idle.

questions.question: What is a Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) Type 2 in dimensional data modeling?
options: Tracking full historical changes by creating a new row for each update with valid start/end timestamps and an active flag
Overwriting existing column values in-place without preserving history (SCD Type 1)
Adding a new column to the table for every change
Deleting historical records older than 90 days
questions.explanation: SCD Type 2 preserves complete historical audit trails by inserting a new record with effective date ranges whenever dimensional attributes change.

questions.question: In Apache Kafka, what is a 'Consumer Group'?
options: A set of consumers that cooperate to consume data from topic partitions in parallel, where each partition is read by only one consumer in the group
A group of users visiting a website simultaneously
A database table storing consumer addresses
A security role granting read access to Kafka topics
questions.explanation: Consumer groups allow horizontal scaling of message consumption by dividing topic partitions across multiple consumer instances.

questions.question: What is the primary architectural feature of modern Cloud Data Warehouses like Snowflake?
options: Decoupled storage and compute, allowing compute clusters to scale up, down, or pause instantly independent of storage volume
Running entirely in memory without persistent storage
Using NoSQL key-value stores exclusively
Requiring manual server hardware provisioning
questions.explanation: Separating compute (Virtual Warehouses) from central cloud storage (S3/Azure Blob) enables elastic scaling and concurrency without resource contention.

questions.question: In dbt (data build tool), what is a 'materialization'?
options: The strategy determining how a dbt model is built in the warehouse (e.g. view, table, incremental, ephemeral)
Converting JSON strings into binary files
Extracting data from an on-premise mainframe
Creating automated visual dashboard charts
questions.explanation: dbt materializations define whether SQL select statements are deployed as database Views, physical Tables, or Incremental updates.

questions.question: What is 'Idempotency' in data pipeline engineering and why is it essential?
options: A pipeline running multiple times with the same input produces the exact same output without creating duplicate or corrupt records
A pipeline that executes in under 1 second
A pipeline that only ingests CSV files
A pipeline that encrypts columns using AES-256
questions.explanation: Idempotent pipelines (e.g. using upserts or partition overwrites) can safely retry after unexpected network or worker failures without duplicating data.
